description:
FILED s543t (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28, on the s543t tree = main 394a0012 + the batch) while probing #2560 / #932's sub half (member 4: scratch/s543t/p/m4-scope.pl row 9 in the s543t worktree).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    sub deep { my $n = shift; "d$n" =~ /(d)(\d+)/; return $n ? deep($n - 1) . ",$2" : "$2" }
    print deep(3), "\n";
    perl: 0,0,0,0     s543t: 0,1,2,3     the base (cababb9d): 0,0,0,0 (by accident: its captures were one global)

perl's model: $1..$N read PL_curpm, the last successful match OP in scope, and the offsets live in that op's regexp.  A sub's exit restores PL_curpm (which op), not the op's data; a recursive call matching through the same op overwrote the data, so the caller reads the inner call's $2.  s543t restores the caller's match STATE (a snapshot taken at the frame's first match, docs/ir-spec.md "Match variables"), which is right for every non-recursive shape (Math::BigRat::new, Text::Wrap, any helper sub) and differs here.

TO MATCH perl exactly the record would have to live on the match op (the p-regex-match struct) and the frame restore the CURRENT-OP pointer -- a representation change of the match state; not worth it for this shape unless a real program needs it.  Flagged in s543t's report as the one shape the #932 fix moved away from perl.

=== s543t review (2026-11-28) === BASE = PERL on this row: a regression by the letter.  The reviewing session's t-01 row 3 (`sub rec { my $n = shift; return "" if !$n; "k$n" =~ /(k\d)/; my $deep = rec($n - 1); "$1$deep" } print rec(3)`): perl k1k1k1, main 655db409 k1k1k1, the s543t tree k3k2k1 -- the base equalled perl by accident (one global match state), the tree restores the caller's own match where perl's op-held captures show the innermost call's.  Kept rare (reading a capture after recursing through the same op).
frequency_reason: known only from s543t's probe; reading $1 AFTER recursing through the same match is perl's surprising answer (perlre warns to copy captures first) -- a working program copies them
subject: SILENT WRONG: a capture variable read after a RECURSIVE call that matched through the SAME pattern op -- perl reads the inner call's match (the captures belong to the op's regexp; only which op is current is restored at sub exit), PCL since s543t the caller's own match
triage_reason: match variables (perlvar) in ordinary sub code; the capture scoping of #932 is IN
